document.title: Intelligent Assets: Autonomous Financial Instruments with Embedded Compliance
document.abstract: We develop a theory of intelligent assets — financial instruments that carry executable programs and a compliance function as intrinsic properties. The programs enable autonomous operation: an intelligent asset can rebalance a portfolio, negotiate trades, migrate between jurisdictions, and file regulatory reports without human intervention. The compliance function — a map from twenty-three regulatory domains to a five-element ordered set — ensures that every autonomous action is evaluated against applicable regulations before execution. We show that the compliance function is fail-closed by construction and that sanctions violations are algebraically non-overridable. Cross-jurisdictional compliance composes through lattice operations, enabling an asset to accumulate sovereign attestations as it moves between jurisdictions. We describe the execution architecture, trace a worked example through the lifecycle of an autonomous private equity fund, and identify the hard open problems.

definitions.label: Definition 2.1
definitions.formal: A = (g, pi, sigma, s, P): genesis document, attestation portfolio, receipt log, persistent storage, bound programs.

definitions.label: Definition 2.2
definitions.formal: J = (E_J, L_J, K_J): evaluator function, content-addressed lawpack, signing key.

definitions.label: Definition 3.1
definitions.formal: T_J(A): D -> S, a function assigning each of 23 compliance domains a state; composition is pointwise meet on the applicable fragment (F135 + F142 + F144).

definitions.label: Definition 3.2
definitions.formal: V(T) = meet over D_req of T[d]. The asset may act iff V(T) is passing.

propositions.label: Proposition 3.1
propositions.statement: If T[Sanctions] = NonCompliant, then V(T) = NonCompliant regardless of all other domains.

propositions.label: Proposition 3.2
propositions.statement: Unevaluated domains default to Pending (non-passing). Absence of attestation blocks action.

limitations.title: The Oracle Problem
limitations.summary: Evaluator correctness unverifiable from within the system.

limitations.title: Bootstrapping
limitations.summary: Requires jurisdictional adoption that has not yet occurred.

limitations.title: Race to the Bottom
limitations.summary: Fraudulent attestations cannot be detected cryptographically.

limitations.title: Agent Alignment
limitations.summary: Who governs the asset's bound programs?

limitations.title: Privacy
limitations.summary: ZK proofs resolve tension only for circuit-expressible predicates.
